fields.product.indication: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

fields.protocol.title: A Phase 2a Study of CNV-512 in Adults with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction

fields.plan.rationale: CNV-512 is an intravenous agent intended to improve exercise capacity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, a condition with no approved disease-modifying therapy. A prior Phase 1 study in healthy volunteers established tolerability across the dose range now proposed.
fields.plan.general_approach: Development moves directly to a Phase 2a study in the target population, using exercise capacity and haemodynamic endpoints to establish proof of mechanism before a larger efficacy study is designed.
fields.plan.first_year_scope: One Phase 2a study in adults with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is planned in the first year following submission.
fields.plan.estimated_enrollment: Approximately 60 participants randomised across two dose levels and placebo.
fields.plan.anticipated_risks: Anticipated risks of particular severity are symptomatic hypotension during and shortly after infusion, and renal function decline observed at supratherapeutic exposures in the 26-week rat study. Blood pressure is monitored throughout infusion and creatinine is a protocol-specified stopping criterion.

planned_studies.title: A Phase 2a Study of CNV-512 in Adults with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
planned_studies.objectives: To assess the effect of CNV-512 on exercise capacity and to evaluate safety and tolerability in the target population.
planned_studies.design: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study with two active dose levels.
planned_studies.population: Adults with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, NYHA class II to III, with an ejection fraction of at least 50 percent.
planned_studies.parameters: Primary endpoint is change in six-minute walk distance. Safety assessed by adverse events, blood pressure, renal function and ECG.
planned_studies.status: Protocol submitted with this Initial IND. Enrolment has not started.
